item.text: {"question_id":"1B.4","answer":"During 2023, Mexico’s state institutions and representatives supported arms-control, disarmament, nonproliferation, verification, and risk-reduction efforts. Mexico was a party to the TPNW, having ratified it in 2018; it authored a 2023 TPNW draft resolution, voted for a UN resolution prohibiting nuclear use, participated in TPNW implementation work, co-organized regional disarmament training, and joined a 1540 implementation peer review. Mexico also issued 2023 diplomatic statements advocating NPT implementation, safeguards, verification, de-alerting, and stronger controls. These records show formal treaty participation and diplomatic advocacy, but they do not establish that López Obrador personally directed the actions, or that Mexico funded, domestically implemented, inspected, enforced, or measurably complied with all relevant obligations during 2023. The supplied evidence therefore supports formal engagement and stated support, with substantial uncertainty about operational implementation and enforcement; later biosecurity baselines are qualifying context only and do not establish 2023
